Paper_Title: Software Testing with Large Language Models: Survey, Landscape, and Vision
Authors: Junjie Wang, Yuchao Huang, Chunyang Chen, Zhe Liu, Song Wang, Qing Wang
Brief_Summary: Foundational survey mapping how LLMs are applied across software testing tasks, from unit test generation to bug analysis, with a landscape and research vision.
Problem_Solved: Lack of a consolidated view of the fast-growing LLM-for-testing field.
Methodology_Short: Systematic survey of 102 papers organized by testing task and LLM usage pattern.

Paper_Title: Large Language Models for Software Engineering: A Systematic Literature Review
Authors: Xinyi Hou, Yanjie Zhao, Yue Liu, Zhou Yang, Kailong Wang, Li Li, Xiapu Luo, David Lo, John Grundy, Haoyu Wang
Venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology (TOSEM)
Brief_Summary: Broad SLR of LLM applications across the software engineering lifecycle, including a substantial testing sub-area, with taxonomies of models, tasks, and data.
Problem_Solved: Fragmented understanding of LLM applications, effects, and limitations across SE.
Methodology_Short: PRISMA-style SLR covering 395+ studies with multi-dimensional taxonomy.

Paper_Title: Foundation Models in Software Engineering: A Taxonomy, Systematic Review, and In-Depth Analysis of Testing Support
Brief_Summary: Systematic review of 224 studies on foundation models across the SDLC, finding heavy concentration on implementation and testing; two-dimensional lifecycle x capability taxonomy.
Problem_Solved: Uneven, poorly characterized adoption of foundation models across SDLC phases.
Methodology_Short: Systematic review of 224 studies with a two-dimensional taxonomy.

Paper_Title: No More Manual Tests? Evaluating and Improving ChatGPT for Unit Test Generation
Authors: Zhiqiang Yuan, Yiling Lou, Mingwei Liu, Shiji Ding, Kaixin Wang, Yixuan Chen, Xin Peng
Venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering / FSE (ACM)
Brief_Summary: First large empirical study of ChatGPT unit test generation; passing tests rival human tests on coverage/readability but many suffer compilation/assertion errors. Introduces ChatTester.
Problem_Solved: Understanding correctness and quality gaps of LLM-generated unit tests.
Methodology_Short: Empirical evaluation on 1000+ focal methods plus an iterative refinement approach (ChatTester).

Paper_Title: An Empirical Study of Unit Test Generation with Large Language Models
Authors: Lin Yang, Chen Yang, Shutao Gao, Weijing Wang, Bo Wang, Qihao Zhu, Xiao Chu, Jianyi Zhou, Guangtai Liang, Qianxiang Wang, Junjie Chen
Brief_Summary: Empirical study of open-source LLMs with varied prompting for unit test generation, comparing against closed-source models and prompting strategies.
Problem_Solved: Under-explored capabilities of open-source LLMs and prompting settings for unit tests.
Methodology_Short: Empirical comparison across multiple open-source LLMs and prompt configurations.

Paper_Title: ChatUniTest: A ChatGPT-based Automated Unit Test Generation Tool
Authors: Zhuokui Xie, Yinghao Chen, Chen Zhi, Shuiguang Deng, Jianwei Yin
Brief_Summary: Tool that parses the project, builds an adaptive focal context within token limits, and validates/repairs ChatGPT-generated unit tests.
Problem_Solved: LLM unit test generation is limited by context window and validation of outputs.
Methodology_Short: Adaptive focal-context construction plus generation-validation-repair loop.

Paper_Title: Automatic High-Level Test Case Generation using Large Language Models
Authors: Navid Bin Hasan, Md. Ashraful Islam, Junaed Younus Khan, Sanjida Senjik, Anindya Iqbal [estimated]
Brief_Summary: Generates high-level (functional) test cases from requirements using GPT-4o, Gemini, LLaMA and Mistral; fine-tuning improves smaller models; human evaluation confirms usefulness.
Problem_Solved: Bridging requirements to high-level functional test cases with LLMs.
Methodology_Short: Multi-model evaluation with fine-tuning and human evaluation survey.

Paper_Title: Generating High-Level Test Cases from Requirements using LLM
Brief_Summary: Two-stage pipeline: LLM first infers applicable test design techniques from a requirement document, then generates high-level test cases per technique.
Problem_Solved: Producing systematic, technique-grounded functional test cases from requirements.
Methodology_Short: Test-design-technique inference followed by per-technique test generation.

Paper_Title: AI-Driven Test Case Generation from Natural Language Requirements
Brief_Summary: Addresses requirements-based test generation directly from NL, tackling ambiguity, traceability, evaluation thoroughness, and hallucination control.
Problem_Solved: Ambiguity and imprecision when deriving tests directly from NL requirements.
Methodology_Short: Framework with emphasis on ambiguity handling, traceability and hallucination control.

Paper_Title: A Tool for Test Case Scenarios Generation Using Large Language Models
Brief_Summary: Web-based tool using an LLM agent and prompt engineering to generate epics, high-level user stories, and test case scenarios from user requirements.
Problem_Solved: Automating traceable test scenario generation from user requirements.
Methodology_Short: LLM-agent tool with prompt engineering over a user-story pipeline.

Paper_Title: Acceptance Test Generation with Large Language Models: An Industrial Case Study
Brief_Summary: AutoUAT and Test Flow tools generate acceptance test scenarios from user stories and convert them into executable scripts; shows LLMs can improve the UAT process with tooling and supervision.
Problem_Solved: Underexplored application of LLMs to user acceptance testing.
Methodology_Short: Two-step generation of UAT scenarios then executable scripts, with industrial evaluation.

Paper_Title: Streamlining Acceptance Test Generation for Mobile Applications Through Large Language Models: An Industrial Case Study (AToMIC)
Brief_Summary: AToMIC uses specialized LLMs to generate Gherkin scenarios, Page Objects, and executable UI test scripts directly from JIRA tickets and recent code changes.
Problem_Solved: Manual effort in producing executable acceptance tests for mobile apps.
Methodology_Short: Multi-LLM pipeline from requirements/code-changes to Gherkin, POs, and UI scripts; industrial study.

Paper_Title: Multi-Agent Collaborative System for Automated User Acceptance Testing with Large Language Model
Brief_Summary: Proposes a multi-agent collaborative LLM system that autonomously performs user acceptance testing with human-like decision making.
Problem_Solved: Automating UAT end-to-end with collaborating autonomous LLM agents.
Methodology_Short: Multi-agent architecture where LLM agents plan and execute UAT tasks.

Paper_Title: Autonomous Large Language Model Agents Enabling Intent-Driven Mobile GUI Testing (DroidAgent)
Authors: Juyeon Yoon, Robert Feldt, Shin Yoo
Brief_Summary: DroidAgent is an autonomous Android GUI testing agent that sets and pursues semantic tasks using multiple LLM instances plus long/short-term memory, producing executable scenarios.
Problem_Solved: Moving beyond random exploration to intent-driven, semantic mobile GUI testing.
Methodology_Short: Modular multi-LLM agent with memory that autonomously explores and scripts scenarios.

Paper_Title: Make LLM a Testing Expert: Bringing Human-like Interaction to Mobile GUI Testing via Functionality-aware Decisions (GPTDroid)
Authors: Zhe Liu, Chunyang Chen, Junjie Wang, Mengzhuo Chen, Boyu Wu, Xing Che, Dandan Wang, Qing Wang
Brief_Summary: GPTDroid formulates mobile GUI testing as a Q&A with the LLM, making functionality-aware decisions to interact with apps like a human tester and achieve higher coverage/bug detection.
Problem_Solved: Random/model-based GUI testing lacks human-like semantic understanding.
Methodology_Short: LLM-as-tester Q&A loop with functionality-aware prompting on real Android apps.

Paper_Title: Are Autonomous Web Agents Good Testers?
Authors: Antoine Chevrot, Alexandre Vernotte, Jean-Remy Falleri, Xavier Blanc, Bruno Legeard [estimated]
Brief_Summary: Evaluates whether autonomous web agents (ATAs) can execute manual test cases from NL instructions and deliver verdicts, positioning them as alternatives to brittle scripts.
Problem_Solved: Assessing LLM web agents as autonomous test executors/oracles for web apps.
Methodology_Short: Empirical evaluation of ATA baselines (e.g., SeeAct-ATA) executing and verifying manual test cases.

Paper_Title: Towards Autonomous Testing Agents via Conversational Large Language Models
Authors: Robert Feldt, Sungmin Kang, Juyeon Yoon, Shin Yoo
Brief_Summary: Presents a taxonomy of LLM-based testing agents by autonomy level and demonstrates a conversational testing framework, arguing hallucination can aid test exploration.
Problem_Solved: Framing and structuring how autonomous LLM agents can drive the testing process.
Methodology_Short: Conceptual taxonomy plus a conversational testing framework demonstration.

Paper_Title: WebVoyager: Building an End-to-End Web Agent with Large Multimodal Models
Authors: Hongliang He, Wenlin Yao, Kaixin Ma, Wenhao Yu, Yong Dai, Hongming Zhang, Zhenzhong Lan, Dong Yu
Brief_Summary: WebVoyager is an end-to-end multimodal web agent that completes real-world website tasks, reaching 59.1% success and introducing an automated GPT-4V-based evaluation protocol.
Problem_Solved: Building and evaluating agents that autonomously operate real web interfaces end-to-end.
Methodology_Short: Multimodal (screenshot+DOM) agent with an automated LLM-based success evaluator.

Paper_Title: Test Oracle Automation in the Era of LLMs
Authors: Facundo Molina, Alessandra Gorla, Marcelo d'Amorim [estimated]
Brief_Summary: Examines opportunities and challenges of using LLMs to automate test oracle generation, a key bottleneck for autonomous verification.
Problem_Solved: The oracle problem: deciding correct vs incorrect behavior automatically.
Methodology_Short: Position/analysis of LLM-based oracle generation approaches and open challenges.

Paper_Title: Multi-Agent LLMs for End-to-End Test Generation with Accurate Oracles
Brief_Summary: Multi-agent LLM framework generating end-to-end tests with accurate oracles from NL without fine-tuning or external prefix-generation tools like EvoSuite.
Problem_Solved: Producing correct oracles and complete tests without heavy tooling/fine-tuning.
Methodology_Short: Multi-agent decomposition for test prefix and oracle generation.

Paper_Title: On the Soundness and Consistency of LLM Agents for Executing Test Cases Written in Natural Language
Brief_Summary: Formal study of soundness (false failures from ambiguous NL) and consistency (nondeterministic re-runs) when LLM agents execute NL test cases.
Problem_Solved: Prior work assumes generated cases are the deliverable; this exposes reliability/flakiness risks in the EXECUTION of NL tests — a threat-to-validity the new paper must address for its execution half.
Methodology_Short: See novelty; VERY HIGH — defines the reliability/flakiness challenge of NL-driven test execution agents; key related-work + threats-to-validity citation.

Paper_Title: AI Agents for Web Testing (WebProber)
Brief_Summary: Prototype AI-agent framework that, given a URL, autonomously explores a site, simulates real user interactions, detects bugs/usability issues, and produces human-readable reports.
Problem_Solved: Adds autonomous EXPLORATION + bug/usability detection with human-like interaction, beyond static generation of business-process test cases.
Methodology_Short: See novelty; HIGH — autonomous web exploration and defect reporting is a form of the execution/UAT-agent capability.

Paper_Title: Autonomous Intelligent Agents for Natural-Language-Driven Web Execution with Integrated Security Assurance
Brief_Summary: NL-driven web execution agents that generate Selenium scripts; raises script-generation success 55%->93%, 8x fewer navigation failures, 80% fewer timing races, 75% less test-creation time; integrates security assurance.
Problem_Solved: Goes past generation into robust NL-to-executable-script EXECUTION with quantified reliability gains and security checks — directly relevant to production UAT execution.
Methodology_Short: See novelty; VERY HIGH — end-to-end NL-to-execution pipeline with concrete execution-reliability metrics.

Paper_Title: A Zero-Cost Self-Healing Approach Using DOM Accessibility Tree Extraction (Beyond LLM-based test automation)
Brief_Summary: Replaces per-run LLM discovery with structured accessibility-tree extraction; self-heals only broken selectors (<1s, zero human intervention); scales to 300+ tests at zero ongoing API cost.
Problem_Solved: Prior work does not touch execution maintenance; this tackles brittle-locator self-healing and DOM-abstraction for durable EXECUTION at scale/low cost.
Methodology_Short: See novelty; VERY HIGH — self-healing + DOM/accessibility-tree abstraction are core execution-phase mechanics.

Paper_Title: Practical Limits of Autonomous Test Repair: A Multi-Agent Case Study with LLM-Driven Discovery and Self-Correction
Brief_Summary: Analyzes 300 autonomous execution reports / 636 test-case executions across 10 scenario families; 70% repair-convergence rate, mean 4.4 repair iterations.
Problem_Solved: Provides empirical limits of autonomous self-repair during EXECUTION — grounds realistic expectations for the execution contribution.
Methodology_Short: See novelty; VERY HIGH — quantifies autonomous repair/self-correction during test execution.

Paper_Title: Framework and Benchmark for Code-Driven Agentic Testing in Web Development (CAT)
Brief_Summary: Introduces Code-driven Agentic Testing: agent writes Playwright code to drive the browser, gathers feedback, autonomously explores web apps to find bugs; provides a benchmark for VLM bug-discovery.
Problem_Solved: Introduces a paradigm and BENCHMARK for agentic end-to-end web execution/bug-finding — prior work lacked any execution benchmark.
Methodology_Short: See novelty; VERY HIGH — execution paradigm + benchmark; useful for evaluating the new execution half.

Paper_Title: HxAgent: Iterative Agent Planning for End-to-End Web Application Testing
Brief_Summary: Iterative planning agent for E2E web testing; 97.4% Exact-Match on MiniWoB++, 83.8% EM / 91.8% Prefix-Match on 350 web tasks, beating WALT by 10-13%.
Problem_Solved: Advances autonomous EXECUTION planning accuracy on web tasks well beyond static generation.
Methodology_Short: See novelty; HIGH — iterative execution planning for E2E web app testing.

Paper_Title: LLM-Guided Scenario-based GUI Testing (ScenGen)
Brief_Summary: Five-agent LLM pipeline (Observer, Decider, Executor, Supervisor, Recorder) that maps app business logic to scenario-based GUI tests and executes them.
Problem_Solved: Extends business-logic-aware testing into a MULTI-AGENT EXECUTION loop on mobile GUI, versus prior single-phase generation.
Methodology_Short: See novelty; HIGH — multi-agent architecture spanning perceive->decide->execute->verify; template for execution agents.

Paper_Title: From Business Requirements to Test Assertions: Evaluating LLM-Generated Oracles on Real Bugs
Brief_Summary: Evaluates LLM-generated oracles/assertions derived from business requirements against real bugs; finds oracles align more with requirements than with SUT and show high variance.
Problem_Solved: Directly probes the requirements->oracle path used by the prior generation work, exposing its accuracy limits on real bugs.
Methodology_Short: See novelty; MEDIUM-HIGH — oracle reliability is central to autonomous verdicts in the execution phase.

Paper_Title: Agent-Based Test Assertion Generation via Diverse Perspective Aggregation
Brief_Summary: Agent-based assertion generation that aggregates diverse LLM perspectives to produce stronger, more diverse assertions/oracles.
Problem_Solved: Advances assertion/oracle strength via multi-perspective agents beyond single-model generation.
Methodology_Short: See novelty; MEDIUM — stronger oracles improve execution verdict fidelity.

Paper_Title: Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration for Unit Test Generation via Human-Testing-Inspired Workflows (TestAgent)
Brief_Summary: LLM test generation emulating human testing practice through multi-agent collaboration.
Problem_Solved: Multi-agent, human-workflow-inspired generation vs single-prompt business-process generation.
Methodology_Short: See novelty; MEDIUM — architecture relevance; primarily generation-side.

Paper_Title: DOM Tree Pruning Programming for Web Agent (Prune4Web)
Brief_Summary: Shifts DOM handling from LLM reading of 10k-100k-token DOMs to LLM-generated executable Python scoring scripts that programmatically prune DOM elements.
Problem_Solved: Novel DOM-ABSTRACTION technique that makes execution agents scalable on huge real-world pages.
Methodology_Short: See novelty; HIGH — DOM abstraction/scalability is a core execution-agent bottleneck.

Paper_Title: Manipulating LLM Web Agents with Indirect Prompt Injection via HTML Accessibility Tree
Brief_Summary: Shows adversarial triggers embedded in HTML/accessibility tree can hijack LLM web agents into unintended actions.
Problem_Solved: Introduces a SECURITY threat model for accessibility-tree-based execution agents absent from generation-only prior work.
Methodology_Short: See novelty; HIGH — security/threats-to-validity for DOM/accessibility-tree-driven execution agents.

Paper_Title: The Potential of LLMs in Automating Software Testing
Brief_Summary: Agent-oriented framework generating unit tests, visualizing call graphs, and automating test execution and reporting.
Problem_Solved: Adds automated EXECUTION + reporting to generation, reducing human intervention across the loop.
Methodology_Short: See novelty; MEDIUM-HIGH — explicit generation+execution+reporting automation.

Paper_Title: Evaluating LLMs for Multimodal GUI Test Generation in Android Applications
Brief_Summary: Empirically evaluates multiple LLMs for multimodal (screenshot+DOM) GUI test generation; effectiveness varies by model.
Problem_Solved: Provides recent multimodal GUI-testing evidence and model-comparison the new paper should cite.
Methodology_Short: See novelty; MEDIUM — multimodal GUI grounding informs execution-agent perception.

Paper_Title: KuiTest: Leveraging Knowledge in the Wild as GUI Testing Oracle for Mobile Apps
Brief_Summary: Uses external in-the-wild knowledge as a GUI testing oracle where no executable spec exists (model-parametric oracle).
Problem_Solved: Novel oracle strategy for GUI where prior work had no runtime oracle.
Methodology_Short: See novelty; MEDIUM-HIGH — oracle technique for execution-time verdicts on GUI.

Paper_Title: FlakyFix: Using Large Language Models for Predicting Flaky Test Fix Categories and Test Code Repair
Authors: Sakina Fatima, Hadi Hemmati, Lionel Briand [estimated]
Brief_Summary: Uses LLMs to predict flaky-test fix categories and to repair flaky test code, moving beyond mere flakiness prediction to actionable fixes.
Problem_Solved: Flaky tests non-deterministically pass/fail; little tool support exists to actually fix them.
Methodology_Short: LLM-based fix-category prediction plus code repair, evaluated on flaky-test datasets.

Paper_Title: An Analysis of LLM Fine-Tuning and Few-Shot Learning for Flaky Test Detection and Classification
Brief_Summary: Compares fine-tuning vs few-shot learning of LLMs for detecting and classifying flaky tests, characterizing data/resource tradeoffs.
Problem_Solved: Reliable flaky-test detection/classification with limited labeled data.
Methodology_Short: Empirical comparison of LLM fine-tuning and few-shot learning on flaky-test datasets.

Paper_Title: FlakyGuard: Automatically Fixing Flaky Tests at Industry Scale
Brief_Summary: Automatically repairs reproducible flaky tests at industrial scale, repairing 47.6% with 51.8% developer-accepted fixes and beating prior work by >=22%.
Problem_Solved: Industrial-scale automatic repair of flaky tests to keep CI reliable.
Methodology_Short: LLM-driven flaky-test reproduction and repair pipeline, industrial evaluation.

Paper_Title: Adaptive Test Generation Using a Large Language Model (TestPilot)
Authors: Max Schafer, Sarah Nadi, Aryaz Eghbali, Frank Tip
Brief_Summary: TestPilot uses an off-the-shelf LLM (Codex) to adaptively generate JavaScript unit tests without extra training, achieving 70.2% median statement coverage.
Problem_Solved: Automated unit test generation across languages with poor tool support and low readability.
Methodology_Short: Adaptive prompt-based generation with feedback, evaluated against Nessie on npm packages.

Paper_Title: Multi-language Unit Test Generation using LLMs
Authors: Rangeet Pan, Myeongsoo Kim, Rahul Krishna, Raju Pavuluri, Saurabh Sinha
Brief_Summary: A generic static-analysis-guided pipeline that steers LLMs to produce compilable, high-coverage unit tests across Java and Python, including environment mocking.
Problem_Solved: Generated tests often fail to compile and lack coverage; few languages supported.
Methodology_Short: Static-analysis-guided LLM pipeline (context + mocking) evaluated on Java and Python.

Paper_Title: Coverage-Guided LLM-Based Test Generation (CoverUp)
Authors: Juan Altmayer Pizzorno, Emery D. Berger
Brief_Summary: CoverUp interleaves coverage analysis with LLM dialogs to iteratively raise Python regression-test coverage, beating CodaMosa on line/branch coverage.
Problem_Solved: LLM test generation uses fixed prompts and ignores which code remains uncovered.
Methodology_Short: Iterative coverage-analysis-in-the-loop prompting to target uncovered lines/branches.

Paper_Title: Code-Aware Prompting: A Study of Coverage-Guided Test Generation in Regression Setting using LLM (SymPrompt)
Authors: Gabriel Ryan, Siddhartha Jain, Mingyue Shang, Shiqi Wang, Xiaofei Ma, Murali Krishna Ramanathan, Baishakhi Ray
Brief_Summary: SymPrompt uses symbolic path prompts to guide LLMs, improving correct test generations 5x and coverage 26% (2x on GPT-4) in regression settings.
Problem_Solved: Fixed prompting strategies limit coverage and correctness of LLM regression tests.
Methodology_Short: Symbolic execution-path-aware prompting evaluated on CodeGen2 and GPT-4.

Paper_Title: A Comparative Study of SBST, Symbolic Execution, and LLM-Based Approaches to Unit Test Generation
Brief_Summary: Compares search-based, symbolic-execution, and LLM-based unit test generation; LLMs trail on coverage but lead on mutation score, indicating deeper semantic understanding.
Problem_Solved: Understanding relative strengths of classic vs LLM test generation paradigms.
Methodology_Short: Controlled empirical comparison across three test-generation paradigms.

Paper_Title: Large-scale, Independent and Comprehensive Study of the Power of LLMs for Test Case Generation
Authors: Wendkuuni C. Ouedraogo, Kader Kabore, Haoye Tian, et al. [estimated]
Brief_Summary: Large independent study of LLM unit-test generation across correctness, understandability, coverage, and test smells, comparing to EvoSuite.
Problem_Solved: Fragmented, non-independent evidence on LLM test-generation quality and test smells.
Methodology_Short: Large-scale empirical study over many models/projects benchmarked against EvoSuite.

Paper_Title: Correct and Strong Test Oracle Generation with LLMs (TOGLL)
Brief_Summary: TOGLL generates correct and fault-revealing test oracles with LLMs, detecting 1,023 mutants EvoSuite misses and outperforming TOGA on real Defects4J bugs.
Problem_Solved: The oracle problem: generating oracles that are both correct and strong at finding bugs.
Methodology_Short: LLM-based oracle generation evaluated on mutants and Defects4J real bugs.

Paper_Title: Do LLMs Generate Test Oracles That Capture the Actual or the Expected Program Behaviour?
Authors: Michael Konstantinou, Renzo Degiovanni, Mike Papadakis [estimated]
Brief_Summary: Studies whether LLM-generated oracles encode expected vs actual behaviour; LLMs are better at generating than classifying oracles and benefit from meaningful names.
Problem_Solved: Risk that LLM oracles merely restate current (possibly buggy) behaviour instead of intended behaviour.
Methodology_Short: Empirical study of oracle generation vs classification with fault-detection analysis.

Paper_Title: Retrieval-Augmented Test Generation
Authors: Jiho Shin, Reem Aleithan, Hadi Hemmati, Song Wang [estimated]
Brief_Summary: Investigates RAG for unit-test generation over API docs, GitHub issues, and StackOverflow Q&As, analysing how each knowledge source affects test quality.
Problem_Solved: LLM tests lack grounding in external, domain-specific knowledge.
Methodology_Short: RAG pipeline evaluated across three knowledge sources for ML/DL API tests.

Paper_Title: Generating Test Scenarios from NL Requirements using Retrieval-Augmented LLMs (RAGTAG)
Brief_Summary: RAGTAG uses RAG with LLMs to integrate domain knowledge and generate functional test scenarios from natural-language requirements.
Problem_Solved: Requirements-based test scenario generation needs domain grounding to be accurate.
Methodology_Short: Retrieval-augmented generation of test scenarios from NL requirements.

Paper_Title: Vision-driven Automated Mobile GUI Testing via Multimodal Large Language Model (VisionDroid)
Authors: Zhe Liu, Cheng Li, Chunyang Chen, Junjie Wang, et al. [estimated]
Brief_Summary: VisionDroid aligns GUI text with screenshots into a vision prompt so an MLLM can detect non-crash functional bugs during mobile GUI testing.
Problem_Solved: Detecting non-crash functional bugs that text-only GUI testing misses.
Methodology_Short: MLLM vision+text prompting over app exploration to spot functional GUI defects.

Paper_Title: Towards Test Generation from Task Description for Mobile Testing with Multi-modal Reasoning (VisiDroid)
Brief_Summary: VisiDroid combines images and text so an LLM can generate mobile tests from task descriptions and better judge task completion, reaching 87.3% accuracy.
Problem_Solved: Knowing when a task-driven mobile test has actually completed its goal.
Methodology_Short: Multimodal (image+text) reasoning framework for task-based mobile test generation.

Paper_Title: Large Language Models for Mobile GUI Text Input Generation
Brief_Summary: Systematically evaluates LLMs for generating semantically valid text inputs that unblock automated mobile GUI exploration.
Problem_Solved: Text-input fields block automated GUI exploration when inputs are not semantically valid.
Methodology_Short: Empirical evaluation of multiple LLMs for GUI text-input generation.

Paper_Title: AutoDroid: LLM-powered Task Automation in Android
Authors: Hao Wen, Yuanchun Li, Guohong Liu, et al.
Brief_Summary: AutoDroid combines LLM commonsense with app-specific knowledge from dynamic analysis to autonomously complete arbitrary tasks on any Android app.
Problem_Solved: Prior mobile task automation lacked scalable language understanding and needed manual effort.
Methodology_Short: LLM + automated dynamic analysis to build app knowledge and execute UI tasks.

Paper_Title: DroidBot-GPT: GPT-powered UI-grounded Smartphone Task Automation in Android
Authors: Hao Wen, Hongming Wang, Jiaxuan Liu, Yuanchun Li
Brief_Summary: DroidBot-GPT translates GUI state and available actions into NL prompts and asks a GPT-like LLM to choose actions, automating Android app tasks from NL descriptions.
Problem_Solved: Automating Android UI task execution directly from natural-language goals.
Methodology_Short: GUI-to-NL prompting loop with an LLM action selector on real Android apps.

Paper_Title: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents (WebArena)
Authors: Shuyan Zhou, Frank F. Xu, Hao Zhu, Xuhui Zhou, et al.
Brief_Summary: WebArena is a reproducible, self-hostable web environment with long-horizon tasks used to build and benchmark autonomous web agents that execute and are auto-verified.
Problem_Solved: Lack of realistic, reproducible environments to evaluate autonomous web agents.
Methodology_Short: Functional web environment + task suite with programmatic success evaluation.

Paper_Title: A Versatile and Autonomous Multi-Agent System for Web Task Execution with Strategic Exploration (WebPilot)
Authors: Yao Zhang, Zijian Ma, Yunpu Ma, et al. [estimated]
Brief_Summary: WebPilot is a multi-agent MCTS-based system for autonomous web task execution, achieving SOTA on WebArena and strong MiniWoB++ results with GPT-4.
Problem_Solved: Autonomous multi-step web task execution needs strategic exploration and planning.
Methodology_Short: Multi-agent Monte-Carlo-tree-search planning evaluated on WebArena and MiniWoB++.

Paper_Title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Improve REST API Testing (RESTGPT)
Authors: Myeongsoo Kim, Tyler Stennett, Dhruv Shah, Saurabh Sinha, Alessandro Orso
Brief_Summary: RESTGPT extracts machine-interpretable rules and example values from NL in an API spec, augmenting the OpenAPI spec to drive more effective REST API testing.
Problem_Solved: Informal/insufficient API documentation limits automated REST API test quality.
Methodology_Short: LLM rule/value extraction that enriches OpenAPI specs for downstream testing tools.

Paper_Title: Automated REST API Documentation and Testing via LLM-Assisted Request Mutations (RESTSpecIT)
Authors: Alix Decrop, Gilles Perrouin, Mike Papadakis, et al. [estimated]
Brief_Summary: RESTSpecIT infers REST API documentation and performs black-box testing using LLM-assisted request mutations, without a full OpenAPI spec.
Problem_Solved: REST API testing requires specs that are often missing or informal.
Methodology_Short: LLM-guided request mutation to infer specs and black-box test REST APIs.

Paper_Title: Effective REST API Testing with Small Language Models (LlamaRestTest)
Authors: Myeongsoo Kim, Saurabh Sinha, Alessandro Orso [estimated]
Brief_Summary: LlamaRestTest fine-tunes small language models for REST API testing, matching/exceeding RESTGPT and tools like RESTler, EvoMaster, and ARAT-RL on real services.
Problem_Solved: Large-model cost/latency for REST API testing; can small models suffice?
Methodology_Short: Fine-tuned small LMs evaluated on 12 real services vs SOTA REST testers.

Paper_Title: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues? (SWE-bench)
Authors: Carlos E. Jimenez, John Yang, Alexander Wettig, Shunyu Yao, et al.
Brief_Summary: SWE-bench evaluates whether LLMs can resolve real GitHub issues, requiring patches validated by the repository's own test suites; frontier models solve only the simplest issues.
Problem_Solved: No realistic benchmark for autonomous, test-validated software issue resolution.
Methodology_Short: Benchmark of 2,294 real issues with execution-based (unit-test) validation of patches.

Paper_Title: WebPilot / Epic-Organized vs. Requirement-Aligned Gherkin: An Empirical Evaluation of LLM-Based Acceptance Criteria Generation
Brief_Summary: Evaluates whether epic-organized LLM-generated Gherkin acceptance criteria beat requirement-aligned generation on quality and coverage.
Problem_Solved: Manual authoring of Gherkin BDD acceptance criteria is a requirements-engineering bottleneck.
Methodology_Short: Empirical comparison of two LLM Gherkin-generation strategies for coverage/quality.

Paper_Title: Generating BDD Acceptance Tests using Large Language Models: An Empirical Study
Brief_Summary: Shows GPT-3.5/GPT-4 can generate largely error-free BDD acceptance tests, with few-shot prompting improving accuracy and reducing syntax errors.
Problem_Solved: Automating BDD acceptance-test authoring from requirements with correct Gherkin syntax.
Methodology_Short: Empirical study of prompting strategies for BDD test generation with syntax/validation analysis.

Paper_Title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Software Testing and Inspection Automation
Brief_Summary: Applies a RAG pipeline to reduce hallucination in LLM-driven software testing and inspection by injecting supplementary knowledge sources.
Problem_Solved: LLM hallucination undermines reliability of automated testing/inspection outputs.
Methodology_Short: RAG-augmented LLM framework for testing and inspection tasks.

Paper_Title: Execution-aware, Feedback-driven Regression Testing Generation with Large Language Models
Brief_Summary: Addresses the coverage plateau in LLM regression-test generation by making the LLM execution-aware and feedback-driven about program execution.
Problem_Solved: LLM regression tests stagnate in coverage due to weak reasoning about execution.
Methodology_Short: Execution-feedback loop that informs the LLM to break through coverage plateaus.

Paper_Title: Efficient LLM-driven Test Generation Using Mutant Prioritization (PRIMG)
Brief_Summary: PRIMG prioritizes mutants to guide LLM test generation, reducing test-suite size while maintaining high mutation coverage and outperforming random mutant selection.
Problem_Solved: Generating high-impact tests without exhaustive, costly mutation-driven generation.
Methodology_Short: Mutant-prioritization module feeding an LLM test generator, evaluated on mutation coverage.

Paper_Title: TraceLLM: Leveraging Large Language Models with Prompt Engineering for Enhanced Requirements Traceability
Brief_Summary: TraceLLM uses LLMs with prompt engineering to establish and maintain trace links between requirements and downstream artifacts including tests.
Problem_Solved: Maintaining requirements-to-artifact traceability (incl. tests) is costly and error-prone.
Methodology_Short: Prompt-engineered LLM approach for generating/maintaining requirement trace links.

Paper_Title: On the Diffusion of Test Smells in LLM-Generated Unit Tests
Brief_Summary: Contrasts LLM-generated tests with human suites and EvoSuite to determine whether LLMs reproduce human-like test smells or synthetic artifacts.
Problem_Solved: Understanding maintainability/quality problems (test smells) in LLM-generated tests.
Methodology_Short: Empirical comparison of LLM vs human vs SBST tests for test-smell diffusion.

Paper_Title: LLM-based Low-Level Integration Test Generation for Java (IntTestGen)
Brief_Summary: IntTestGen generates low-level integration tests for Java, improving line/branch coverage and mutation score and covering additional dependency code.
Problem_Solved: Integration testing (beyond isolated units) is under-served by LLM test generators.
Methodology_Short: LLM-based integration-test generation evaluated on coverage and mutation across two benchmarks.

Paper_Title: Test vs Mutant: Adversarial LLM Agents for Robust Unit Test Generation
Brief_Summary: Uses adversarial LLM agents (test-writer vs mutant-maker) to drive robust, high-coverage, compilable unit tests.
Problem_Solved: LLM tests are readable but often low-coverage and non-compilable.
Methodology_Short: Adversarial multi-agent test-vs-mutant loop for robust unit test generation.

Paper_Title: Enhancing Test Suite Robustness via LLM-Based Generation and Genetic Optimization (EvoGPT)
Brief_Summary: EvoGPT hybridizes LLM test generation with evolutionary search to produce diverse, bug-revealing unit tests.
Problem_Solved: LLM-only generation lacks diversity and bug-revealing power of search-based methods.
Methodology_Short: Hybrid LLM + genetic-algorithm framework for unit test generation.

Paper_Title: A System for Automated Unit Test Generation Using Large Language Models and Assessment of Generated Test Suites
Authors: Andrea Lops, Fedelucio Narducci, et al. [estimated]
Brief_Summary: Builds a scalable system and a Methods2Test-derived dataset to compare LLM-generated tests with human-written tests and assess quality.
Problem_Solved: Need for scalable systems and datasets to fairly assess LLM test-suite quality.
Methodology_Short: Automated generation system + new dataset + evaluation methodology.

Paper_Title: Exploratory Study on Private GPTs for LLM-Driven Test Generation in Software and Machine Learning Development
Brief_Summary: Uses acceptance criteria from epics/stories with private GPTs to produce testable criteria and tests in software and ML development settings.
Problem_Solved: Turning story/epic acceptance criteria directly into testable artifacts with private LLMs.
Methodology_Short: Exploratory study of private-GPT-driven test generation from acceptance criteria.

Paper_Title: A Systematic Literature Review on Large Language Models for Automated Program Repair
Authors: Quanjun Zhang, Chunrong Fang, Yang Xie, et al.
Brief_Summary: PRISMA-style SLR of LLM-based automated program repair, including the tight coupling between test-based validation and repair.
Problem_Solved: Fragmented understanding of LLM-based APR techniques and their test-driven validation.
Methodology_Short: Systematic literature review of LLM-for-APR studies and methods.

Paper_Title: Enhancing Conversation-Based Automated Program Repair via Contrastive Test Case Pairs
Brief_Summary: Improves conversational LLM program repair using contrastive test-case pairs to better localize and validate fixes.
Problem_Solved: Conversational APR needs stronger test-driven feedback signals to converge.
Methodology_Short: Contrastive test-case-pair feedback within a conversational APR loop.

Paper_Title: Correct and Strong REST API Testing with Verified LLM-Inferred Dependencies and Response-Driven Refinement
Brief_Summary: Validates LLM-inferred REST operation dependencies via execution and refines test sequences from responses, avoiding spurious/infeasible tests.
Problem_Solved: LLM-inferred API dependencies are often unvalidated, yielding infeasible test sequences.
Methodology_Short: Execution-verified dependency inference plus response-driven test-sequence refinement.

Paper_Title: LLM-as-a-Judge for Scalable Test Coverage Evaluation
Brief_Summary: LLM-as-a-Judge (LAJ) is a rubric-driven framework producing structured JSON verdicts to evaluate Gherkin acceptance-test coverage at scale.
Problem_Solved: Assessing acceptance-test coverage quality at scale is a QA bottleneck.
Methodology_Short: Rubric-driven LLM judging framework with structured JSON outputs for coverage evaluation.

Paper_Title: Semantic-Aware Gray-Box Game Regression Testing with Large Language Models (SAGE)
Brief_Summary: SAGE uses LLM semantic analysis of update logs to prioritize regression tests most relevant to version changes, evaluated on Overcooked Plus and Minecraft.
Problem_Solved: Regression testing must adapt test selection efficiently as software/game versions change.
Methodology_Short: LLM-based semantic change analysis for test prioritization in gray-box game testing.

Paper_Title: WebTestPilot: Agentic End-to-End Web Testing against Natural Language Specification by Inferring Oracles with Symbolized GUI Elements
Authors: Xiwen Teoh, Yun Lin, Duc-Minh Nguyen, Ruofei Ren, Wenjie Zhang, Jin Song Dong
Brief_Summary: Neurosymbolic LLM agent for E2E web testing vs NL spec: symbolizes GUI elements into variables and infers pre/post-condition oracles capturing data/temporal/causal deps; 99% task completion, 96% precision/recall.
Problem_Solved: Implicit oracle inference + hallucination-vs-real-bug in autonomous web test execution.
Methodology_Short: Symbolization layer + NL-to-steps with inferred pre/post-condition oracles; bug-injected benchmark.

Paper_Title: Compiling Large Multi-Modal Requirement Documents into Runnable Software Systems: From an Agentic Test-Driven Perspective
Authors: Weiyu [et al.], Xiwen Teoh, Duc-Minh Nguyen, Ruofei Ren, Jiaxin, Haoxu, Haoyu, Yun Lin [estimated]
Brief_Summary: Agentic test-driven compilation of large multi-modal requirement documents into runnable systems; tackles requirement scaling and omitted constraints.
Problem_Solved: LLM performance degrades on multi-modal docs with hundreds of scenarios.
Methodology_Short: Agentic, test-driven decomposition of large requirement documents.

Paper_Title: Generating Project-Specific Test Cases with Requirement Validation Intention
Authors: Binhang Qi, Xinyi, Yuhuan, Chenyan [et al.], Yun Lin [estimated]
Brief_Summary: Generates project-specific test cases guided by requirement validation intention.
Problem_Solved: Aligning generated tests with the validation intent behind requirements.
Methodology_Short: Requirement-validation-intention-driven test generation.

Paper_Title: Generalizing Test Cases for Comprehensive Test Scenario Coverage (TestGeneralizer)
Authors: Binhang Qi, Xinyi, Chenyan [et al.], Yun Lin [estimated]
Brief_Summary: TestGeneralizer: understand requirement/scenario, build scenario templates and instances, then generate/refine executable tests for broad scenario coverage.
Problem_Solved: Insufficient test-scenario coverage from focal-method-only tests.
Methodology_Short: Three-stage scenario-template generation and executable test synthesis.

Paper_Title: Design-to-Action Agents for GUI Testing
Authors: Ruofan Liu, Xiwen Teoh, Guanjie, Ruofei Ren, Yun Lin [estimated]
Brief_Summary: Agentic GUI testing mapping design intent to concrete UI actions.
Problem_Solved: Bridging design intent and executable GUI actions for testing.
Methodology_Short: Design-to-action agent architecture for GUI testing.
